Alternaria leaf spot.cause: Fungal disease (Alternaria helianthi), spreads in warm humid conditions, often via infected plant debris or wind-borne spores
Alternaria leaf spot.treatment: Remove and destroy infected leaves; apply a labeled fungicide (e.g. chlorothalonil or mancozeb based, verify locally approved products); avoid overhead irrigation to reduce leaf wetness; practice crop rotation
Alternaria leaf spot.severity: moderate to high if untreated - can cause significant leaf loss and yield reduction

Downy Mildew.cause: Oomycete pathogen (Plasmopara halstedii), favored by cool wet conditions, often soil-borne or seed-borne
Downy Mildew.treatment: Use disease-resistant seed varieties where possible; apply metalaxyl-based seed treatment preventively; improve field drainage; remove infected seedlings early
Downy Mildew.severity: high - can cause systemic infection and significant stand loss if it strikes early

Powdery Mildew.cause: Fungal disease (Golovinomyces/Erysiphe species), favored by warm dry days with high humidity at night, common late in the season
Powdery Mildew.treatment: Apply sulfur-based or other labeled fungicide at first sign; improve air circulation via proper plant spacing; avoid excess nitrogen fertilization which promotes susceptible new growth
Powdery Mildew.severity: moderate - mainly reduces photosynthetic efficiency rather than causing rapid plant death

Wilted leaf.cause: Can result from multiple stresses: fungal/bacterial wilt pathogens, water stress, or root damage - visual wilting alone does not confirm a specific pathogen
Wilted leaf.treatment: Assess soil moisture and irrigation first; if disease is suspected, inspect stem/root for discoloration and consult local agricultural extension for pathogen-specific diagnosis
Wilted leaf.severity: variable - depends on underlying cause, ranging from temporary water stress to serious vascular disease

Healthy.treatment: No action needed - continue standard monitoring and care
